title: Observation of even-denominator fractional quantum Hall states at $ν= 3/4$ and 5/4 in the lowest Landau level
authors: Siddharth Kumar Singh, Chengyu Wang, Adbhut Gupta, Kirk W. Baldwin, Loren N. Pfeiffer, Mansour Shayegan
abstract: Two-dimensional electron systems (2DESs) confined to wide GaAs quantum wells provide a unique platform to study exotic fractional quantum Hall states (FQHSs) because the 2DES has a bilayer charge distribution with significant interlayer tunneling. Precise control over the 2DES density allows the tuning of the interlayer tunneling over a wide range. Here, we present our discovery of new even-denominator FQHSs in the lowest Landau level (orbital index \textit{N} = 0) at filling factors $ν= 3/4$ and 5/4 in an ultrahigh-quality 2DES confined to a 72.5-nm-wide GaAs quantum well. The ground states at $ν= 3/4$ and 5/4 both evolve from composite fermion Fermi seas to FQHSs as the density is raised so that interlayer tunneling is sufficiently reduced and the 2DES becomes two-component, signaled by the behavior of the FQHSs flanking $ν= 3/4$ and 5/4. The two-component nature of the $ν=3/4$ and 5/4 FQHSs is also evident from their extreme sensitivity to the bilayer charge distribution symmetry: both states disappear quickly when the charge distribution is made asymmetric by only $\simeq 2\%$. We find a natural explanation for the 3/4 and 5/4 FQHSs in terms of two states linked by particle-hole symmetry, and using the Scarola-Jain bilayer composite fermion framework which is a generalization of the well-known, two-component, Halperin state ($Ψ_{331}$ state). Our observations elucidate the crucial role of competing energy and length scales in wide quantum wells in stabilizing new ground states.
summary: This paper reports the discovery of stable even-denominator Fractional Quantum Hall States at $\nu=3/4$ and $5/4$ in GaAs quantum wells. The findings are explained by a theoretical model involving two-component bilayer composite fermions, highlighting that these states rely critically on maintaining symmetry in the electron charge distribution.
main_problem: The research focuses on discovering and characterizing novel even-denominator Fractional Quantum Hall States (FQHSs) at filling factors $\nu=3/4$ and $5/4$. These states are studied in the context of wide quantum wells exhibiting bilayer characteristics.
main_result: Robust even-denominator FQHSs are observed, which are explained by a two-component, bilayer composite fermion framework. The stability of these states is highly dependent on maintaining charge distribution symmetry.
method: The study combines low-temperature transport measurements ($R_{xx}, R_{xy}$) with theoretical modeling using composite fermion theory and analyzing the system's response to controlled charge asymmetry.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a two-dimensional electron system (2DES) confined in wide GaAs quantum wells, which naturally supports a bilayer charge distribution. The physics is governed by strong Coulomb interactions and tunable interlayer tunneling.
key_observables: Longitudinal resistance minima ($R_{xx}$), energy gaps ($\nu\Delta$), and the critical charge asymmetry $(\Delta n/n)_C$ required to destabilize the FQHSs.
important_parameters: Filling factors $\nu=3/4, 5/4, 3/2$; interlayer tunneling strength ($\alpha$); charge distribution symmetry ($\Delta n/n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the FQHSs can be described by generalizations of composite fermion wavefunctions (e.g., Scarola-Jain bilayer framework).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $R_{xx}$ and $R_{xy}$ traces confirming FQHS plateaus at $\nu=3/2, 5/4,$ and $3/4$, and show how these states evolve or disappear when the charge distribution symmetry is intentionally broken.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the experimental observation of even-denominator FQHSs in wide QWs. It then develops a theoretical explanation linking these states to bilayer composite fermion physics, detailing their dependence on interlayer tunneling and charge symmetry.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed experimental evidence for exotic correlated electron phases (FQHSs) that emerge due to the interplay between orbital quantization (Landau levels), strong Coulomb interactions, and structural degrees of freedom (bilayer coupling).

(b) Self-consistent Schr¨odinger and Poisson (Hartree) calculations for the charge distribution and potential in a 72.5-nm-wide GaAs QW, showing the effect of changing the density (n) and the charge distribution asym- metry (∆n/n) using the front and back gates. (c) Measured ∆SAS in our sample plotted as a function of n. The shaded, red region marks the range relevant for the data presented in this manuscript.

FIG. 2. (a,b) Rxx (black) and Rxy (blue) traces taken at T ≃33 mK, for a 72.5-nm-wide GaAs sample with n = 1.83 and 1.59, respectively. Strong even-denominator FQHSs are observed at ν = 3/2, 5/4, and 3/4. Spontaneously imbalanced, bilayer FQHSs are observed in close vicinity of the 5/4 and 3/4 FQHSs at ν = 19/15 and 11/15, respectively. Vertical lines mark the expected positions of the odd- and even-denominator FQHSs, and horizontal lines mark the expected positions for the Hall plateaus.
FIG. 3. Arrhenius plots of the Rxx minima at ν = 3/2 (blue), 5/4 (red) and 3/4 (green) FQHSs at n = 1.83, allowing us to extract their energy gaps as indicated in the upper right corner.

FIG. 4. Evolution of the ground state at ν = 3/4 from a CF Fermi sea to a FQHS as the density is raised. Rxx traces are shifted vertically for clarity. The 2DES becomes 2C at high density, signaled by the disappearance of the 1C, odd- numerator FQHSs at ν = 5/7 and 7/9, and the emergence of 2C, bilayer FQHSs at ν = 6/7, 29/35, and 11/15. The layer fillings ¯ν1 and ¯ν2 associated with the observed FQHSs are shown above the figure.

FIG. 5. Evolution of the 2DES around ν = 3/2 and 5/4 as the density is raised. For clarity, Rxx traces are shifted vertically. With increasing n, the states at ν = 3/2 and 5/4 evolve from compressible Fermi seas to incompressible FQHSs. 1C to 2C transitions can be observed at the even-numerator ν = 4/3 FQHS at n = 1.73, and the ν = 6/5 FQHS at n = 1.69. The odd-numerator FQHSs at ν = 11/7, 7/5 and 9/7 become weak or disappear, while new FQHSs emerge at ν = 19/15 and 29/21 at n = 1.83.
